sources.institution: Foundation Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe

evidence.estrutura: Benário was a committed communist revolutionary associated with the Comintern and disciplined party organization. This supports strong collective political organization rather than libertarian decentralization, although her personal writings do not provide a detailed federalism theory.
evidence.representacao: Her revolutionary communist politics were not centered on liberal parliamentary democracy and accepted extra-parliamentary insurrection. This places her below liberal-democratic maximalism, while her anti-fascism strongly opposes racial dictatorship.
evidence.poder: She participated in revolutionary underground activity and accepted disciplined political struggle, but was herself a victim of authoritarian imprisonment, deportation and Nazi murder. Evidence supports a complex position: tolerance for revolutionary state power alongside absolute opposition to fascist coercion.
evidence.imigracao: As a German Jewish exile active internationally and later deported from Brazil, her life strongly reflects opposition to racist exclusion and nationalist persecution. This supports an internationalist, non-xenophobic orientation rather than restrictive assimilation.
evidence.diplomacia: Her politics were internationalist and tied to transnational communist networks, but she was not a conventional diplomat. Her orientation was revolutionary international solidarity rather than pacifist interstate diplomacy.
evidence.intervencao: Her revolutionary activity included support for armed insurrection and political struggle abroad, placing her away from non-interventionism despite anti-fascist motivations.
evidence.economia: As a communist activist, she supported abolition of capitalist ownership and a collectively organized socialist economy. This strongly supports public/collective ownership.
evidence.controle: Her Marxist-Leninist political environment favored coordinated socialist planning rather than laissez-faire markets.
evidence.comercio: Communist internationalism rejects capitalist free trade but not in favor of nationalist tariff protection; use a managed/planned international economic orientation rather than classic protectionism.
evidence.religiao: Her political identity was secular communist, and there is no basis for religious governance. This strongly supports secular public institutions.
evidence.moral: Her anti-fascism, internationalism and opposition to racial persecution support egalitarian social values, though she was not a theorist of the later cultural issues in this axis.
evidence.tecnologia: Her politics emerged from industrial modernity and revolutionary modernization but she left no distinctive technology doctrine. Use a moderate pro-modernization position.
